newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's lower house approves corporate tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's lower house approves corporate tax bill.

text.p: Nepal's lower house of parliament has adopted a bill limiting corporate tax to 20 percent, officials said on Friday.
Currently, Nepal does not have a fixed corporate tax. The Finance Minister sets the tax each year in the country's annual budget.
Officials said the tax was recently cut to 25 percent from 33 percent last year but could have easily been raised next year in the absence of the new legislation.
The Industrial Enterprises Act, adopted by the lower house late on Thursday, needs the approval of the upper house of parliament before becoming law.

Nepal, one of the world's least developed countries, opened up its economy in 1992 to attract foreign investment in the key areas of hydro-electric power, tourism and labour-intensive manufacturing to create employment.
Officials said foreign investment of over 11 billion rupees ($193.8 million) in about 350 projects have been approved by the government.

Foreign investors point to high business visa fees of $100 a month, a lack of coordination between government departments, power shortages and high electricity tariffs as constraints to outside investment in Nepal.

Nepal's House of Representatives passed the bill by voice vote. The bill gives an additional 50 percent tax concession to "national priority" industries such as nursing homes and hospitals, transport infrastructure, fuel saving and pollution control, and traditional medicines.
